sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Internet Retailing of Outdoor Sports and Camping Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong commercial/corporate overlay influenced by Spanish legal tradition and international financial-market practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), effective 31 October 2012
Canada–Panama Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)
Panama–Spain Agreement for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (APPRI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Ley de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales, Financiamiento del Terrorismo y Financiamiento de la Proliferación de Armas de Destrucción Masiva), as amended, in particular by Ley No. 70 de 2017; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 128 de 2016 and Decreto Ejecutivo No. 163 de 2016 regulate beneficial-owner information and the depository of bearer shares; the Central Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) is administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under UAF regulatory guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport for each director, officer, shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of residence / national passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issuing country is a party; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the state of incorporation of the corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Panama Resident Agent and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the principal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / financial institution due-diligence certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and, if required by the receiving authority, Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence under Ley 23/2015; screening of all directors, shareholders, officers and beneficial owners against the UAF national PEP list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, and EU consolidated financial sanctions list; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification is obligatory for any UBO meeting the 25% threshold; positive PEP/sanctions matches require the AML Compliance Officer's written approval and, where applicable, a Suspicious Transaction Report to the UAF within the statutory time limit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sistema de Denominaciones y Servicios en Línea (www.registro-publico.gob.pa), complemented by Panama Emprende (www.panamaemprende.gob.pa) for one-stop commercial incorporation procedures
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; Spanish is the official registry language, but commercial names may be registered in English or another Romanized language provided the legal suffix 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima' is included. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Spanish or English at the time of filing, and the Registro Público retains discretion to request a certified translation when the name is not readily intelligible in Spanish.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANCO, BANK, BANCA, FINANCIERA (requires Superintendencia de Bancos approval)
SEGUROS, REASEGUROS, INSURANCE (requires Superintendencia de Seguros approval)
FONDO, FIDEICOMISO, TRUST (restricted and subject to securities/supervisory approval)
COOPERATIVA (requires Instituto Panameño Autónomo Cooperativo approval)
BOLSA, MERCADO DE VALORES, CORREDOR DE VALORES (requires Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores approval)
HOSPITAL, CLÍNICA, FARMACIA (requires Ministerio de Salud approval)
UNIVERSIDAD, INSTITUTO SUPERIOR (requires Ministerio de Educación approval)
CRUZ ROJA, NACIONES UNIDAS, ESTADO, GOBIERNO, PRESIDENCIA (prohibited as official or international emblems)
FUNDACIÓN (restricted due to conflict with the Private Interest Foundation law)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Registro Público, the applicant or its resident agent may file a written motion for reconsideration ('recurso de reconsideración') with the Dirección General del Registro Público within five (5) business days from notification. If denied, a second-instance appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be lodged before the First Superior Civil Court of Panama within five (5) business days. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately re-file a different name template without penalty. A granted name reservation may be extended once for a further 30-day period upon written request submitted during the final five (5) business days of the original window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The statutory registered office of a Panama S.A. must be a physical address in Panama and is commonly the address of the licensed resident agent. Virtual-office or digital-mailbox addresses may be used for commercial correspondence, billing, and administrative services, but cannot replace the physical statutory address of the registered agent. A Panama e-commerce company conducting no local physical operations is not required to lease a separate commercial premises; however, if the taxpayer becomes registered for 'Aviso de Operación' or VAT, the DGI and the relevant municipality may require proof of a physical establishment for the declared business address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a low-risk internet-retailing entity with no physical inventory, employees, or fixed place of business in Panama, the estimated probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months is 5–7%. This risk increases to approximately 15% if the company registers for General Occupational License ('Aviso de Operación') or obtains a VAT (ITBMS) registration, as DGI and municipal authorities occasionally perform desk-based and physical verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff (arancel) for a single name search and reservation certificate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarization of the Pacto Social / Articles of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public in the Republic of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee scale under Panamanian notarial law plus attorney drafting fee at prevailing market rate for a standard S.A. package.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate registration in the Public Registry (inscripción)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry fee computed by authorized-capital bracket and number of subscribers; estimated for a standard USD 10,000 authorized capital S.A.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year UBO registry filing and mandatory AML/CFT due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / licensed resident agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual beneficial-owner statement and enhanced KYC/EDD compliance fee charged by the licensed agent in accordance with UAF regulations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate in Panama for professional corporate domiciliation, typically USD 350–700 per year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization package for the corporate due-diligence bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores or competent foreign apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat per-document statutory fee of approximately USD 20–40 per authentication, plus documentary handling and courier costs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copy of the public incorporation deed (Personería Jurídica) for the post-registration legal file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Issuance tariff for certified copies of registered corporate deeds.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Law 32 of 1927, as amended), Articles 1, 2, 5, 13 and 24; complementary provisions of the Código de Comercio.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas, Sección de Sociedades Anónimas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución and Pacto Social
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. At least one share must be subscribed and issued. Paid-in capital may consist of cash or assets and may be credited in the corporate records; no mandatory escrow or public deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE INCORPORATION BOARD OF DIRECTORS. The directors, acting as the first Board of [Company], S.A., pursuant to the Ley General de Sociedades, resolve that: 1. All subscriptions to the authorized shares set forth in the Escritura Pública de Constitución are accepted, and the Secretary shall issue share certificates to the subscribers. 2. The registered office of the Company shall be at the address maintained by the resident agent. 3. The individuals listed in the schedule are appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer, to serve until the next annual general meeting with all powers granted by law and the bylaws. Approved and adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Plataforma de Reserva de Nombres de Sociedades
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application for the proposed corporate name and an alternative name through the Public Registry's name search module. Verify absence of identical, phonetically similar, or confusingly similar registered companies. The Registry issues a name reservation certificate valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Application for name reservation (formulario de reserva de nombre)
Identification documents of initial incorporators/shareholders
Proof of payment of administrative name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the alternate name is automatically considered; if the rejection is due to an alleged conflicting mark, the incorporators may file a written reconsideration request with the Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas supported by evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Incorporation Deed Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian notary to draft and formalize the Escritura Pública de Constitución and Pacto Social. The deed must specify corporate name, registered office, authorized share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, reserved rights, board structure, and registered agent. All incorporators or attorneys-in-fact must appear before the notary to execute the deed; the notary authenticates it and issues certified copies.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft Escritura Pública de Constitución and Pacto Social
Valid passports or identity cards of shareholders
Power of attorney if signature is by an authorized representative
Registered agent appointment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defective clauses, the parties execute a corrective addendum (subsanación) restating the affected clause; if a signature is challenged, re-execution is effected before the same notary with original identity documents or a certified power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Public Deed at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Oficina de Sociedades Anónimas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución with the Public Registry together with the fiscal registration form and proof of payment of the applicable registry fee. The Registry legally reviews the deed, records it in the Mercantile Section, and assigns the corporate file number (ficha). Legal personality is acquired as of the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Original certified copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Receipt for registration fee and stamp tax
Formulario de inscripción de sociedad
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns the deed with correctable defects, the applicants must submit a corrective deed or clarifying note through the same notary; unresolved objections may be appealed to the Director General del Registro Público within five working days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Appointment of Corporate Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Sociedad Anónima and Resident Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organization meeting of the newly incorporated company's board. The directors adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution accepting the share subscriptions, fixing the adopted registered office address, appointing the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, and approving the corporate records book. The minutes are inserted in the corporate minutes ledger and signed by all attending directors.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes
Share subscription and certificate book
Officer acceptance forms
Corporate statutory books (stock ledger and minutes book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting minutes contain omissions or are not unanimously signed, the directors may cure the deficiency by executing a unanimous written consent resolution or by convening a new board meeting to ratify the full text.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Municipal Operation Notice and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad de Panamá – Dirección de Avisos de Operación; Caja de Seguro Social (CSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Sociedad Anónima with the DGI via the Sede Virtual portal or in person to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), including the fiscal address. File the municipal Aviso de Operación with the municipality where the business operates. If employees will be hired, register the corporation as employer with the CSS and with the Ministry of Labor for occupational safety.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by the Public Registry
Notarized appointment of officers and identification copies
DGI RUC registration application form
Municipal Aviso de Operación application
Lease agreement or proof of place of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality queries the application due to missing proof or signatures, the applicant may supplement the file with the missing documents; administrative reconsideration is available within fifteen days under Ley 38 de 2000.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá – Dirección de Avisos de Operación, coordinated with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias for import/export commercial formalities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Business Operating License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación y Monitoreo Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Registro Ambiental General for low-impact retail/commercial storage activities in an established urban area; no full environmental impact statement required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by internet retailing of camping equipment. Sanitary effluents must comply with applicable municipal sewer connection and discharge rules. Solid waste, including returned or damaged camping equipment, batteries, and packaging, must be handled pursuant to Ley 77 de 2021 (Integrated Solid Waste Management), municipal collection ordinances, and MiAMBIENTE technical guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire prevention and safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural/occupancy clearance from the Dirección de Obras de la Municipalidad de Panamá for the office or warehouse; employer occupational health and safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) and employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama — taxpayer portal and e-services: SIME (Sistema Integrado de Mejora de Ingresos), accessible via https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Sociedad Anónima obtains a Panamanian RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) by: (1) incorporating at the Registro Público de Panamá and recording the directors, resident agent, and secretaries; (2) appointing a Panamanian resident agent and fiscal/legal representative (mandatory for a foreign-controlled company) to interface with the DGI; (3) submitting the RUC application via SIME/DGI with: apostilled/consularized articles of incorporation and public deed, registered bylaws and power of attorney, identity documents of shareholders/directors (cédula or passport), the ISIC 4791 e-commerce activity descriptor, the registered-office or resident-agent address, and bank references; (4) receiving the DGI RUC certificate and assigned ISR/ITBMS obligations; (5) enrolling in the electronic-invoicing system (Factura Electrónica) and activating the SIME digital-certificate account; and (6) where the company maintains no physical Panamanian establishment for pure offshore e-commerce, the DGI registers the S.A. on an ITBMS/invoicing-only footing with the fiscal agent as authorized recipient of DGI notifications. Registration must be completed before taxable operations commence and no later than the statutory deadline (generally 30 days from the start of activities).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope — a Panamanian S.A. is a limited-liability juridical person taxed on its Panamanian-source income (ISR at the standard 25% corporate rate for internal-source profits); foreign-source income, including export e-commerce turnover earned and performed outside Panama, is statutorily outside the Panamanian tax base under the territoriality principle. The entity is not eligible for pass-through treatment; no CFC or worldwide-income aggregation applies in the absence of a Panama permanent establishment for the foreign sales channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not maintain a US-style check-the-box regime and has not enacted OECD hybrid-mismatch elections. The available statutory mechanisms for the S.A. are: (a) an advance tax ruling (consulta fiscal) before the DGI confirming the foreign-source/export character of cross-border web-retail turnover; (b) election of the simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen Especial de Pequeños Contribuyentes) for gross turnover within the legal ceiling (currently up to B/. 150,000 per annum) — available for ISIC 4791 retailers qualifying as 'pequeño contribuyente'; (c) election for the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007, as amended, where the Panamanian entity performs qualifying regional headquarters/co-ordination services for the cross-border group; (d) designation as a registered exporter with the foreign-trade authorities to secure 0% ITBMS and customs facilitations; and (e) tax-neutral classification elections for investment funds or trusts are not applicable to this S.A. structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panama's VAT-equivalent sales tax, governed by Ley No. 13 de 1995 and the Código Fiscal, complemented by distance-selling/e-commerce DGI resolutions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No numeric registration threshold: any person habitually transferring movable goods or rendering services in Panama must register for ITBMS from the first taxable transaction (Código Fiscal and Ley No. 13 de 1995). For non-resident e-commerce sellers, ITBMS registration is triggered by habitual sales to Panamanian consumers (activity-based nexus); a separate numeric VAT registration threshold has not been codified. A simplified quota regime (Régimen Especial de Pequeños Contribuyentes) applies to taxpayers with annual gross turnover not exceeding B/. 150,000, but export sellers and importers are generally excluded from that election. Postal/courier import de minimis of B/. 100 applies to goods entering Panama by mail/express.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory national electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica para Facturas Electrónicas 'FELe') under Ley No. 9 de 2021 and DGI implementing resolutions. Registered businesses must: (1) issue sales documents only through DGI-certified software or the free SIME billing portal; (2) transmit each e-invoice in XML to the DGI in near real-time before the document may be delivered to the buyer; (3) obtain from the DGI a Sello Digital (digital stamp) and Código de Seguimiento (tracking code); (4) complete the invoice with electronic signature and QR; (5) for exports, issue the 'Factura de Exportación' with the 0% rate code and attach the customs DUA reference; (6) integrate ERP/marketplace billing through certified APIs (SIME REST/TLS) for high-volume e-commerce; and (7) retain all stamped e-documents in the SIME repository. Invoices lacking the DGI stamp are legally invalid and input ITBMS credits are denied.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero per cent ITBMS applies to: (i) tangible goods physically exported from Panama, evidenced by the DUA exit stamp, transport document, and payment evidence; (ii) services sold to non-residents and effectively used wholly outside Panama; and (iii) goods supplied to the Colon Free Zone and other qualifying free-zone/licensed warehousing regimes. For the outdoor-camping e-commerce model, the S.A. may zero-rate only the portion of turnover physically shipped from Panama to foreign customers under matching DUA/B-L records; drop-ship orders fulfilled from third-country warehouses to customers outside Panama are treated as non-Panamanian transfers and fall entirely outside the ITBMS base rather than being 'zero-rated export supplies'.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduana - DUA) filed through the SISDUA electronic customs platform with proof of the effective exit of goods from Panama
Commercial invoice and packing list (DGI-stamped e-invoice coded 'Exportación' at 0% ITBMS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or courier despatch proof) showing the foreign destination and physical movement
Exporter enrolment (Registro de Exportadores) and any transport/export permit required for the goods
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT credit advice, or bank deposit evidence showing collection of the export proceeds from the foreign buyer
E-commerce platform sales records, marketplace payout reports, and order-shipping trace logs substantiating each zero-rated web order
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and the Dirección General de Aduanas jointly audit export zero-rating claims through data analytics that cross-match DUA exits, Bills of Lading, shipping manifests, bank remittances, and platform/payment-rail records (PayPal/Stripe settlement data). Circular payments, shell addresses, mismatched quantities, over-invoicing, or fictitious franking trigger recharacterization of the supply as Panamanian-source taxable turnover. Consequences include: (i) reassessment of 7% ITBMS together with any ISR due on the reclassified income; (ii) a monthly surcharge of 1% of the omitted tax up to the legal cap and moratory interest at the statutory rate; (iii) administrative fines under the Código Fiscal ranging from B/. 100 to B/. 50,000 and up to 200% of the tax prejudiced; (iv) forfeiture of export input credits and suspension of the exporter registration; (v) criminal liability for tax fraud (defraudación tributaria — imprisonment of 3 to 6 years) and customs document fraud; and (vi) extension of the statutory clawback/assessment window where returns were not filed or evidence is fraudulent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as banking regulator; Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) as state fiscal agent and clearing bank; Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) as fiscal policy authority. Panama has no conventional central bank and does not issue domestic fiat currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de facto dollarization (U.S. Dollar legal tender; Balboa only a nominal unit). No exchange-control apparatus exists. Current-account transactions (e-commerce collections, trade payments, services) and capital-account transactions (equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend remittances) are freely convertible without prior approval. Profit remittances face no withholding, timing, or repatriation hurdles under the territorial tax model, provided the S.A. remains in good standing and files informative returns with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or export-proceeds repatriation requirement. USD and foreign-currency e-commerce receipts may be retained overseas or remitted at the entity's discretion; the only applicable obligations are bank AML/KYC documentation of source and purpose.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with e-commerce settlement sub-ledger
Operational Account and USD clearing via New York correspondents

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as complementary rail; Low as primary account. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Payoneer, Mercury, DLocal) may serve as ancillary collection and payout rails for Stripe/PayPal settlement corridors, but cannot substitute for a licensed Panamanian bank account because deposit-taking from the public requires a license under Banking Law (Decree-Law 9 of 1998, as amended by Law 79 of 2019). SBP and correspondent banks classify unlicensed EMIs as higher-risk pass-through accounts, generating enhanced scrutiny and potential 'unlicensed banking operation' concerns under FATF/GAFILAT expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Face-to-face interview is generally mandatory for at least one authorized signer/director under SBP customer due diligence rules (Agreement No. 5-2016, as amended). Banco General, Multibank, and Towerbank now accept hybrid/video-remote opening for qualified non-resident clients when original documents are apostilled, local counsel certification is provided, and the applicant maintains a relationship with the bank's international desk. Purely remote opening without any in-person touchpoint remains rare for a Panama S.A. and is generally unavailable to newly formed entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: nominee shareholders, Private Interest Foundation (PIF) intermediate holding, or legacy bearer-share structures trigger enhanced due diligence under Law 70 of 2019 and SBP CDD rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled UBO declaration; certified copy of the public registry ficha (copia literal); full chain of title from incorporation to current shareholders; economic substance statement evidencing operational e-commerce activities; clean sanctions and PEP screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce payment flow flagged as potential 'transaction laundering': card-not-present activity, cross-border Stripe/PayPal settlements, elevated refund rates, and multiple acquiring merchants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreements and onboarding letters from Stripe and PayPal; 12-month settlement and payout statements; reconciliation of Shopify transaction logs; fulfillment and shipping invoices (DHL/FedEx/UPS); refund and chargeback ratios below card-network thresholds; customer service records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch when injecting USD capital or when revenue concentration from one marketplace exceeds 80% of total inflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or internally certified profit and loss statements; prior-year bank statements; supplier contracts and purchase orders; customs and import documentation; Panama informative tax returns with filing acknowledgement; sworn source-of-funds affidavit executed before a Panamanian notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or sanctions hit on a beneficial owner, or nexus to a high-risk jurisdiction within the Latin American e-commerce corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and adverse-media search reports (Refinitiv/LexisNexis/Wolters Kluwer); AML mitigation memorandum from local counsel; board minutes documenting compliance oversight or director changes; evidence of physical operating substance or lawfully disclosed foreign business origin.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) originator board resolution authorizing equity subscription or shareholder loan; (2) SWIFT MT103 transfer in USD from the shareholder's bank to the S.A., using the Panamanian bank's SWIFT BIC and ABA correspondent routing through New York (BNY Mellon, JPMorgan, or Citibank) via Fedwire/CHIPS; (3) reference line coded 'Capital Contribution – BPM6 Code 810 (Direct Investment Equity)' or 'Shareholder Loan – BPM6 Code 824'; (4) inbound credit verified by the bank's compliance team against the approved KYC file before funds are made available; (5) retained documentation: debit/credit advices, SWIFT MT103 confirmation, notarized capital-escrow accounting, and updated corporate ledger entries.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 for routine supplier and logistics disbursements in USD (and selected EUR/GBP payouts through correspondent banks); MT700 documentary commercial letters of credit for high-value inventory purchase orders from Asian, U.S., or EU manufacturers; MT202 cover payments for interbank settlements. All outbound payments pass through bank-side anti-fraud filters and are tagged with 'GROS' (goods/services) or 'TRAD' trade purpose codes. Alternative rails: Stripe/PayPal payout-to-local-bank settlement and commercial card programs for marketplace refunds and upstream disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/CAD) with tenors up to 12 months
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs EUR/GBP) for structural payment-timing mismatch hedging
OTC vanilla FX options (collars and zero-premium structures)
FX swap (swap-forward) structures for short-term USD treasury position funding
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settlement currencies lacking liquid deliverable markets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax / Sole Annual Corporate Fee (Tasa Única Anual de la Sociedad Anónima)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 May of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory interest and surcharges; remaining outstanding for three consecutive years enables administrative strike-off and cancellation in the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta — Form 101)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; a calendar-year S.A. must file by 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing subjects the S.A. to Fiscal Code fines and monthly interest on assessed tax, suspension of tax compliance certificates, and enforcement of outstanding liabilities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary Update (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales / RUBC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of the initial RUBC filing; a share transfer or change in beneficial ownership likewise requires declaration within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false filing carries graduated fines under Law 52 of 2016, commonly from USD 200 to USD 5,000, and persistent non-compliance may block registry certificates and DGI clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Resident Agent Continuity and Annual Service Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent required under Article 54 of Law 32 of 1927; identity recorded at the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous annual obligation; the agent must be maintained without lapse and the service contract renewed on or before the 31 May government-fee deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent resignation without a qualified successor suspends active registry status, restricts transactional filings, and can lead to administrative strike-off of the S.A.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A non-operating Panama S.A. has no automatic annual audit obligation. The DGI can require an independent certified public accountant's report where the taxpayer is classified as large, where annual Panama-source gross revenue exceeds USD 1.5 million, or where total assets exceed USD 3 million; regulated financial and insurance companies are audited under sector-specific rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama has adopted IFRS as the statutory financial reporting framework; non-public small and medium-sized enterprises may apply IFRS for SMEs. The Fiscal Code requires accounting records sufficient to determine taxable Panama-source income, and books are customarily kept in Spanish or in bilingual Spanish-English form.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once every 12 months the S.A. must confirm its final beneficial ownership in the DGI's RUBC. Any transfer of shares must be recorded in the share register and reported to the RUBC within 30 days, and the annual confirmation is required even when no shareholding change occurred. The registered agent must obtain a signed beneficial-ownership schedule from the directors and retain the underlying supporting records.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – USD 400 per annum for standard registered office and resident agent coverage
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable unless the DGI statutory audit threshold is met; when an audited report is required, a certified audit for a single-entity internet-retail S.A. typically ranges from USD 1,500 to USD 4,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to standard S.A. engaged in ISIC 4791 internet retailing. Panama's territorial system excludes foreign-source income, so overseas online sales are effectively taxed at 0%. Preferential regimes (SEM, Zonas Libres, Panama Pacifico) may reduce the effective rate only if the entity obtains special authorization; none is presumed here.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 401 (Declaración de Renta) filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal at the Dirección General de Ingresos (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after fiscal year-end. For calendar-year companies, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, registered name, RUC number, and fiscal year period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reflect the Panamanian resident agent and the exact beneficial ownership structure; foreign directors must be identified and their passports or TRCs recorded in the corporate file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income from sales and services occurring in Panamanian territory
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue generated from Panamanian customers, local warehousing, or in-country delivery. Foreign e-commerce sales are territorially excluded and should be booked separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt and non-taxable income, including foreign-source income under territorial rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a breakdown of foreign-source revenue by jurisdiction and provide intercompany agreements proving the place of contract negotiation, risk assumption, and delivery if audit disputes arise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible cost of goods sold and direct costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate costs to Panama-source revenue using audited internal accounts and arm's-length transfer pricing for cross-border inventory purchases from related suppliers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, including rent, staff, logistics, payment gateway fees, and local advertising
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses effectively incurred to generate Panama-source income; foreign management fees require a robust economic substance file and transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after cost deductions and statutory loss carryforward (maximum 5 years)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that any loss carryforward arises from Panama-source activities only; losses attributable to foreign operations are not eligible in the Panamanian return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual calculated income tax at the 25% headline rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate; territorial exclusions lower the base but do not alter the statutory rate. Check eligibility for deferred advance payment credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments and withholdings made during the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the quarterly advance payments (B/.2% of gross revenue where applicable) and any withholding certificates received from Panamanian customers or platforms.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 1% of the unpaid tax per month or fraction, up to a maximum of 15%; default interest of 1% per month also accrues. Administrative fines under Articles 712 and 760 of the Código Fiscal range from B/.500 to B/.5,000. Understatements exceeding 30% of the correct tax attract a penalty of 50% of the tax evaded, rising to 150% for fraudulent conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must deliver a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its residence tax authority to the Panamanian withholding agent before the dividend distribution. The withholding agent must retain the TRC, complete the DGI withholding schedule at the treaty rate, and file it in the applicable period. If the TRC is not timely submitted, the statutory 10% withholding applies and the shareholder may file a refund claim with the Dirección General de Ingresos, subject to limitation periods.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panama-source withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 12.5%. Under Panama's limited tax treaties (including Mexico, Korea, and certain CARICOM arrangements), royalty withholding may be reduced to 10% and interest to 0%-5% for financial institutions, provided the beneficiary substantiates beneficial ownership and submits the required TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File obligations arise when the taxpayer's annual gross income exceeds B/.1,500,000 (US$1,500,000) and the taxpayer conducts controlled transactions with related parties. The Dirección General de Ingresos may also require documentation below the threshold for transactions involving low-markup distributions, buy-in of goods, or persistent losses.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Law 254 of 2019 and its regulatory decrees impose Economic Substance Requirements on Panamanian legal entities undertaking 'Relevant Activities' within the Republic. An internet retail operation in ISIC 4791 is likely a distribution activity if inventory is held, processed, or delivered from Panama. In such cases, the S.A. must prove physical premises, adequate personnel, executive management in Panama, and annual local expenditure proportional to the income derived from that relevant activity. If all online sales are generated and executed outside Panama with no Panama-source income, the ESR filing is dormant, but the DGI and financial authorities retain audit powers over actual substance versus paper registration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately misclassifying Panamanian domestic e-commerce sales as foreign-source income to avoid the 25% corporate income tax, or inflating cost allocations to erode the Panama-source tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge of 50% to 150% of the underpaid tax, monthly interest penalties, and loss of deductions. Criminal liability under Article 714 of the Código Fiscal and Law 23 of 2017 can expose the company to fines of up to US$250,000 and imprisonment of responsible parties for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced when the S.A. is a mere conduit. Directors and officers can be held jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and penalties, may face criminal prosecution, travel bans, asset freezes, and debarment from holding directorial roles in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Panamanian S.A. without any physical office, employees, or decision-making presence while booking substantial online sales, and failing to file the annual Economic Substance Notification or Report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties under Law 254 of 2019 range from US$75,000 to US$1,000,000 per infraction, plus potential cancellation of the corporate license and dissolution of the entity. False or incomplete ESR filings carry additional fines and may trigger criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false ESR declarations assume statutory responsibility; proven participation in a sham structure allows DGI to assess the unpaid taxes directly against the directors, impose civil restitution, obtain travel bans, and seek imprisonment in aggravated money-laundering cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating internet payment rails (Stripe, PayPal, cards) without implementing risk-based customer due diligence, failing to identify beneficial owners, or permitting unverified third-party funds to flow through the S.A. bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's Law 23 of 2015 and related AML regulations, serious breaches can result in fines up to US$1,000,000, suspension of bank relationships, revocation of payment acceptance authorizations, and administrative closure of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate money laundering risk criminal conviction with imprisonment of up to 12 years, seizure of personal assets, and prohibition from future financial or corporate management roles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Panama-source profit by purchasing inventory from a related supplier at above-arm's-length prices or paying management fees to a foreign affiliate without adequate functional analysis, Local File, or Master File when the annual threshold of B/.1,500,000 is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may recharacterize the controlled transaction, compute taxable income under the arm's-length principle, disallow excessive deductions, and apply a 20% penalty on the additional tax determined, alongside interest and potential criminal penalties for fraudulent documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false intercompany pricing or maintain deficient TP files can be held personally liable for the resulting tax adjustment when the S.A. cannot pay; civil restitution, travel restrictions, and director disqualification may follow.
